senses.gloss: m.radish, the soft tuber of the radish.
units: <cite ref="Berakhot 36a">Ber. 36ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Eruvin 28b:18-19">Erub. 28ᵇ</cite> <he>צנון … אדעתא דפ׳</he> the radish is planted for the sake of the tuber (to be eaten before it is hard and woody).
<cite ref="Chagigah 15a:7">Ḥag. 15ᵃ</cite> <he>עקר פ׳ ממישרא וכ׳</he> (Elisha ben Ăbuya) tore a radish out of the ground on the Sabbath.

<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 10a:15">Ab. Zar. 10ᵃ</cite>. Y. ib. II, 41ᵃ bot.; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 8:3:15">Y. Ter. VIII, 45ᵈ</cite> top, v. <cite ref="N01003"><he>נְעַץ</he></cite>; a. e.—Pl. <he>פּוּגְלִין</he>.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Bava Batra 9:5:4">Y. B. Bath. IX, 17ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Peah 7:3:13">Y. Peah VII, 20ᵇ</cite> top <cite ref="Q00055"><he>פיג׳</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 67">Gen. R. s. 67</cite> <he>שרי עקר פ׳ רברבין וכ׳</he> he (Rabbi) began to tear out the large radishes and plant small ones (intimating to Antoninus the necessity of removing the old officers and appointing new ones); <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 115:22">Yalk. ib. 115</cite>; a. e.
